free_tier.stated: Simple VPS from EUR 1.00/month in Bucharest, Romania: VPS 0.75 gives 0.5 vCore, 768MB RAM, 10GB storage and 500GB bandwidth. VPS 1 is EUR 1.50 for 1 vCore, 1GB RAM, 20GB storage and 1TB bandwidth; VPS 2 is EUR 3.00 for 2 vCores, 2GB RAM, 40GB storage and 2TB bandwidth; VPS 4 is EUR 6.00 for 2 vCores, 4GB RAM, 80GB storage and 3TB bandwidth. Every server gets a 1 Gbit/s port, 1x IPv4 plus IPv6 /56, daily backups (+20% of the plan price, last 5 kept), VNC and serial console, and reverse DNS; the CPU depends on the node: Intel Xeon Gold 6154, Xeon Gold 6132, Xeon Silver 4116 or AMD EPYC 7543.

egress.terms: outbound only, throttled to 100 Mbit/s after the monthly quota with no overage charge
egress.free_allowance: 3 TB per month on VPS 4; 500 GB on the EUR 1.00 plan

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: a control panel with VNC, serial console and reverse DNS is named, plus a documented cloud API on the separate cloud product; no CLI is mentioned for Simple VPS
chaining: EUR 6.00 for 4 GB and 80 GB with 3 TB of outbound and a stated throttle instead of a surprise invoice is the most predictable bandwidth row among documented hosts, and the EUR 1.00 plan is the cheapest machine here of any size; the Romanian location is the only site, so latency to Western Europe is the trade

limits.value: each plan carries a monthly allowance and then drops to 100 Mbit/s until the next month, with no overage charge: 500 GB on VPS 0.75, 1 TB on VPS 1, 2 TB on VPS 2 and 3 TB on VPS 4. That is the unusual case where the post-quota behaviour is stated, and it is a throttle rather than a stop, so the counter binds and then the port does.
